records.people: José Jardim (member of the Board of Directors / Financial Economic Director, CBCS, 2017 to 30 June 2025)
records.move: from Financial Economic Director and board member of the Centrale Bank van Curaçao en Sint Maarten to Chief Executive Officer of Banco di Caribe (effective 1 July 2025)
records.summary: The Curaçao Chronicle reports that Jardim, a CBCS board member since 2017 responsible for financial and economic supervision and monetary policy, became CEO of the commercial bank Banco di Caribe effective 1 July, ending an eight-year tenure at the central bank. The same report settles the ownership of the employer: Banco di Caribe has been wholly owned by United Group Holdings, a privately held group headed by Curaçao businessman Gregory Elias, since 2022. The CBCS Supervisory Board's own announcement of his departure effective 30 June 2025 states only that he would assume a leadership position at a commercial bank, without naming it.
records.source_title: José Jardim appointed new CEO of Banco di Caribe (Curaçao Chronicle)
records.quote: Jardim's appointment marks the end of his eight-year tenure at CBCS, where he has been a board member since 2017.

records.kind: state audit office audit of the bank
records.summary: The State Audit Office (Drzaven zavod za revizija) audited the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia's 2003 financial statements, auditing on site from 12 October to 20 December 2004 under article 2 of the Law on State Audit. Its final report, number 11-107/8 of 4 March 2005, has a section headed improper and unlawful use of funds: it found the National Bank had guaranteed a domestic bank with foreign-currency deposits, and that in January 2004 the foreign banks drew 20,759,515 US dollars from the National Bank's guarantee deposit. It also found that 30,210 thousand denars of purchases, 35.61 percent of the purchases audited, were made without following the Public Procurement Law, and told the bank to give up commercial activities that article 83 of the Law on the National Bank does not allow it.

records.kind: law change the bank objected to in writing
records.summary: Samoa's government pressed ahead with changes to the central bank's law that would widen the Finance Minister's role and move some of the bank's rules into regulations. In a letter to the Attorney-General's office the Central Bank of Samoa said the changes had come as a surprise and warned they could weaken its independence, increase political influence and create legal uncertainty. The IMF wrote to Finance Minister Mulipola Anarosa Ale Molio'o on 9 April 2026 warning the reforms could weaken the bank's autonomy; Prime Minister Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt rejected the warnings as outside interference.
records.source_title: Samoa government pushes bank reforms despite IMF concerns (Pacific Media Network)
records.quote: This government can make its own decisions on what is best and what should be done.

records.category: lending to government beyond legal limits
records.people: John Rolle (Governor, Central Bank of The Bahamas)
records.summary: The Bahamian government drew down $232.3 million of IMF special drawing rights held through the Central Bank of The Bahamas in December 2022. The opposition's finance spokesman Kwasi Thompson said the advance was contrary to section 21 of the Central Bank Act, which sets limits on how much the bank may lend or advance to the government, and the government then tabled a bill stating that section 21 would not apply to the transaction and deemed to have come into force on 1 December 2022. Governor John Rolle said in early January that a memorandum of understanding between the bank and the Ministry of Finance stipulated a change to the Central Bank Act.
records.source_title: Come clean on $232m loan made lawful retroactively (The Tribune, Nassau)
records.quote: They did in fact have a loan or advance from the Central Bank that was contrary to the law.

records.category: audit finding on state debt payments (central bank as paying counterparty)
records.summary: A performance audit of government debt servicing carried out by the Samoa Audit Office in 2014 found instances where repayments of government debt had been delayed, comparing due dates with the actual dates the payments were made by the Central Bank of Samoa. The audit also recorded that there was no formalised arrangement between the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank, and its recommendations were directed at the Ministry of Finance, including that the two bodies formalise their responsibilities. No wrongdoing by any person is alleged in the report as described.

records.quote: The audit team highlighted instances where delays of debts repayments had occurred.
